stem: Tipu Sultan set up his capital at –
expl: Tipu Sultan made Srirangapatnam his capital, and here French officers established the Jacobin Club (it was a branch of the Jacobin Club established in France; Tipu Sultan supported this club and is also said to have become its member). He (Tipu) planted a Tree of Liberty in his capital as a symbol of friendship between France and Mysore. Tipu Sultan sent his missions to Arabia, Constantinople (modern Istanbul), Kabul and Mauritius in order to establish friendly relations with contemporary foreign states and to obtain their support against the British.

stem: The Treaty of Mangalore was signed between Tipu Sultan and the British East India Company in the year
expl: The Treaty of Mangalore between Tipu Sultan and the British East India Company was signed in 1784. In this treaty, the Second Mysore War (1780–84) came to an end.

stem: Englishmen made the Treaty of Srirangapatnam with–
expl: The Third Anglo–Mysore War (1790–92) ended with the Treaty of Srirangapatnam (March,1792). In this treaty, Cornwallis represented the British side and Tipu Sultan represented Mysore. According to its terms, Tipu had to cede nearly half of his territory to the British and their allies, and he also had to pay three crore rupees to the British as war indemnity. The treaty further provided that until Tipu paid about three crore rupees (330 lakh rupees), his two sons would remain in British custody. After this treaty, Cornwallis remarked—“We have effectively crippled our enemy without making our friend too formidable.”

stem: Ranjit Singh got the famous Kohinoor diamond from-
expl: Punjab was a part of Ahmad Shah Abdali’s empire, but after his death in 1772, except for a few smaller regions like Multan and Kashmir, the rest came under the control of the Sikh Misls. Meanwhile, due to internal conflicts among the Afghans, Ranjit Singh got an opportunity to strengthen his position. In 1803, Ahmad Shah Abdali’s grandson Shah Shuja ascended the throne of Kabul, but his brother Shah Mahmud, with the help of powerful Barakzai chiefs—Fateh Khan and Dost Mohammad Khan deposed him in 1809 and himself captured Kashmir and Peshawar. On this occasion, Shah Shuja sought Ranjit Singh’s help to regain the throne of Kabul and presented him with the Koh-i-Noor (Kohinoor) diamond.

expl: Before its establishment at the all-India level, the Hindu Mahasabha was formed at the provincial level. First, in Punjab province, the Punjab Hindu Mahasabha was established in 1909. The Hindu Mahasabha was founded in April, 1915 at the Kumbh Mela in Haridwar under the name “Sarvadeshik Hindu Sabha”. In 1921, the name of this organization was changed to “Akhil Bharatiya Hindu Mahasabha”.
